key_insight: A store-level reinforcement learning policy learns to adapt dispatch objective weights from delayed marketplace feedback, improving batching efficiency while preserving delivery quality.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a production-safe way to tune a combinatorial dispatch optimizer in large-scale delivery systems using offline learned policies and operational safeguards.
method: Learn a discrete weight multiplier at the store level instead of replacing the existing optimizer.
Train a shared value function from centralized offline logs with decentralized execution.
Use Double Q-learning targets plus a conservative regularizer to limit out-of-distribution overestimation.
evidence_signal: In a production switchback experiment, the offline-trained policy increased batching and reduced courier-side time costs without degrading customer-facing delivery quality.
watch_item: Because feedback is delayed, noisy, and coupled across agents, careful offline evaluation and safeguard design are needed to avoid unstable or overconfident policy updates.
paper_title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Marketplace Feedback for Objective-Weight Adaptation in Three-Sided Dispatch
